                    ### Question
                    A 26-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Two weeks ago, he was treated in the emergency department for head trauma after being hit by a bicycle while crossing the street. Neurological examination shows decreased taste on the right anterior tongue. This patient's condition is most likely caused by damage to a cranial nerve that is also responsible for which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Uvula movement
opb. Facial sensation
opc. Eyelid closure
opd. Tongue protrusion
ope. Parotid gland salivation

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's decreased taste on the right anterior tongue suggests damage to cranial nerve VII (facial nerve), which is responsible for taste sensation in this area. Cranial nerve VII also innervates the parotid gland, contributing to salivation. Therefore, the correct answer is that cranial nerve VII is responsible for parotid gland salivation, aligning with the consensus that this nerve has both sensory (taste) and autonomic (salivation) functions.
